BiblicalUsage: Nachats means to be urgent or to press hard, and its only occurrence is David in a hurry. In 1 Samuel 21:8 David asks Ahimelech for a spear or a sword, because the king's business required haste, and he has brought neither sword nor weapons with him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe urgency shows what a person trusts, because David in a hurry runs to the priest and not to his own sword; haste is not the same as panic when the errand is the king's.
